transcript.content: Hello, welcome to the clinic. Can you tell me what's been bothering you or what brings you in today?

I guess I’ve just been really tired lately. I mean, I know teaching is tiring, so I don’t want to make it sound dramatic, but it feels like more than the usual end-of-the-day exhaustion. Even if I sleep through the night, I still have to really push myself to get through grading, making dinner, and getting ready for the next morning.
Have you been feeling this way most of the day, nearly every day, for at least the past two weeks?

Yeah… I think so. I mean, I don’t want to overstate it, but it’s been most days and for a lot of the day. I’m just tired all the time—not just normal teacher-tired. Even if I get a full night’s sleep, I still have to push myself through grading, dinner, and getting ready for the next morning.
Have you noticed a decrease in your interest or pleasure in activities you usually enjoy, like hobbies, socializing, or even teaching?

I’m not sure… I mean, I still try to do the things I’m supposed to do, and I don’t want to say I don’t enjoy anything. I guess I haven’t really paid close attention to that part. Teaching still matters to me, and I do show up for people, so… I’m not sure if I’d call it a loss of interest exactly.
Have you found yourself taking less pleasure in things you used to enjoy, even if you still do them?

I’m honestly not sure. I still do things when I’m supposed to, and I wouldn’t want to make it sound like I don’t care about anything. Maybe I don’t notice the enjoyment as much because I’m just focused on getting through the day, but… I don’t know if that counts as taking less pleasure.
Have you been feeling down, sad, or hopeless most of the day, nearly every day, for the past two weeks?

Yeah… I think so. I can usually still smile for my students and get through the lessons, so it’s not like I’m crying all day or anything. But underneath, most days, there’s this kind of gray, flat feeling that follows me home. Even things like my garden or watercolors feel sort of far away, if that makes sense.
Have you noticed any changes in your appetite or weight recently—like eating a lot less or more than usual, or losing or gaining weight without trying?

I don’t think so… not in any big way. My appetite seems pretty normal, or at least I haven’t noticed a clear change. My clothes fit about the same, so I don’t think I’ve lost or gained much weight. Is that the kind of thing you mean?
Have you noticed yourself moving or speaking more slowly than usual, or on the contrary, feeling restless or fidgety more than usual?

I don’t think I’ve noticed that, no. I mean, I get tired, but I don’t think people would say I’m moving or talking slower than usual. And I’m not especially fidgety either… at least not that I’m aware of. Is that okay to say if I’m not sure?
Have you been feeling unusually guilty about things, or felt like you’re not worth much, or that you’ve let people down, even if you know it might not be rational?

A little, yeah… I mean, I know it’s probably not completely rational. But I keep thinking I should be handling everything better than I am. Like when my lesson plans take twice as long as they should, or when I say no to helping mentor a newer teacher, I end up telling myself I’m letting people down—my family, my school. I don’t want to sound dramatic, but that thought comes up more than I’d like.
Have you noticed any trouble thinking clearly, concentrating, or making decisions lately—like when you're planning lessons or reading something that requires focus?

I don’t think I’ve noticed anything major there. I mean, teaching always takes focus, and some days I have to reread things or sit with decisions a bit, but I wouldn’t say it’s a clear problem lately. At least… not more than I’d expect with a normal busy workload. Is that helpful, or are you looking for something more specific?
Have you found yourself thinking about death or dying more often lately—or even had thoughts about not wanting to live anymore?
No… I don’t think so. I mean, I get discouraged sometimes, but I haven’t been thinking about death or not wanting to live. That’s not really where my mind goes. Is that… the kind of thing you mean?
Can you recall if there have been times recently when activities you used to enjoy, like your garden or watercolors, felt less satisfying or meaningful, even for a while?

Yeah… I think so. Not all the time, and I can still, you know, function—I can smile with the kids and get through my lessons. But then I come home and there’s this kind of gray, flat feeling underneath everything. Even things like the garden or doing watercolors can feel… far away, like I know I usually care about them, but it doesn’t really reach me the same way. Does that make sense?

Even though you still do things like teaching or working on your garden, have you noticed that you’re getting less enjoyment out of them than you used to—like they feel more like tasks than things you look forward to?

Yes… I think that’s fair to say. I don’t want to make it sound like I can’t enjoy anything, because I do keep up with things, and with my students I can still smile and get through the day. But underneath, most days, there’s this kind of gray, flat feeling that follows me home.

So with the garden or my watercolors, it’s not that I hate doing them or anything… they just feel farther away, like more of something I “should” do than something I’m really drawn to. Is that answering what you’re asking?
Have you completely stopped doing any of the activities you used to enjoy, even ones that were important to you, because they no longer feel worth the effort or seem pointless?

Completely stopped… no, I don’t think I’d say completely. I mean, I’m still showing up for my students and my family, and I don’t want to make it sound worse than it is.

But I have pulled back from some things. Like mentoring newer teachers, or saying yes to social outings… I used to do more of that, and lately it just feels like too much effort. And the creative routines I used to have, like making time for painting or those little things that made life feel fuller, I’ve let them slide more than I’d like to admit.

So not pointless exactly… just harder to justify doing, if that makes sense.
Have you noticed that you’ve lost interest in almost everything, even things you used to really care about, like your teaching, your family, or your hobbies?

No… I wouldn’t say I’ve lost interest in almost everything. That sounds stronger than what I mean.

I still care about my teaching and my family. I do. It’s just that some things don’t feel as easy to enjoy, or I don’t feel as pulled toward them as I used to. But I don’t want to overstate it—I haven’t stopped caring about everything. Does that make sense?
